justification.synthesis_rationale: Starting from a modest base rate (8%), we apply a moderate upweight for the petition risk and three downward pressures from margin, precedent, and formalization. The net effect yields a central estimate around 15%, with a wide range to reflect uncertainty and potential late-breaking developments, including the possibility of a successful petition if irregularities are proven and accepted by the court. Given the known factors, the probability remains low but not negligible; the range captures the tail of potential reversals while acknowledging prevailing trends.

question: Will the official result of the Lamag by-election (Sabah), scheduled for January 24, 2026, be overturned before May 1, 2026?
summary: Baseline ensemble probability is 3%, but objections identify a nonzero, albeit small, pathway for overturn via petition processes.
Large margin and subsequent swearing-in of the winner reduce the practical likelihood of reversal before May 1, 2026.
Sabah petition history shows overturns are uncommon; most petitions are dismissed or do not alter outcomes.
The threshold analysis indicates overturn before the target date is unlikely, supporting a modest upward adjustment rather than a dramatic shift.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections correctly flag nonzero risk from petitions, but historical context and the large victory margin imply only a modest upward adjustment rather than a substantial revision.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted probability to 0.05 with a range of 0.04 to 0.08 to reflect nonzero petition risk while not overstating overturn likelihood given current evidence.

([nst.com.my](https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/regional/2026/02/1383883/bns-harun-durabi-keeps-bengkoka-seat-election-court-strikes-out?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Official swearing-in and formal seating reduces overturn likelihood in practice
causal-factors.rationale: Mohd Ismail Ayob was sworn in as Lamag assemblyman on February 10, 2026, reinforcing the legitimacy of the result and raising the hurdle for any petition to overturn. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/02/10/new-lamag-assemblyman-mohd-ismail-officially-sworn-in-at-sabah-assembly/208704?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Active Sabah election petitions in other seats (Sindumin, Pintasan, Bengkoka, etc.)
causal-factors.rationale: petitions have been filed in Sabah and related seats, indicating a nonzero overturn risk, but actual reversals remain rare.

causal-factors.rationale: GRS signaling they will not contest Lamag reduces contest dynamics and potential grounds for overturn.

causal-factors.rationale: With the by-election result declared on Jan 24, 2026, any petition would need to be filed within weeks; the absence of credible challenges reported by early March lowers overturn probability.
